Prattle

PRAT-ul · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To prattle is to talk at length in a foolish way.

The kindergartners prattled on about their pets and their favorite cartoons the entire bus ride home, not really expecting anyone to answer.

Worked Example

The twins prattled happily about their sandcastle plans the entire drive to the beach, switching topics every few seconds.

Their chatter was cheerful and harmless but also aimless and trivial -- exactly the light, childlike quality that separates prattle from more serious or annoying rambling.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

chatter: To chatter is to talk quickly and lightly about unimportant things -- friends chatter before class. To prattle adds a childlike, one-way quality: prattling runs on and on, expecting no real reply. Chatter is light small talk between people; prattle is a happy, trivial stream from one mouth.

babble: To babble is to talk in a rambling way that is genuinely hard to follow -- the words tumble out faster than they organize. Prattling is easy to follow; it is just trivial and childlike. Babble loses the listener in muddle; prattle only risks losing their interest.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

deliberate: to speak carefully and thoughtfully

Where it sits · how far the talk drifts from sense — chat → prattle → blather

chat vs. prattle: To chat is simply to talk casually; to prattle adds a note of childlike, aimless triviality.

blather vs. prattle: Blather goes further still than prattle, describing rambling that sounds outright confusing or nonsensical rather than just light and trivial.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Prattle likely comes from a Low German word imitating the sound of quick, light chatter -- its very sound mimics the rapid, trivial talk it describes.

Use the root in a new word: prate

Use the root in a new word: prate: Prate is an older, closely related word for the same kind of foolish chattering -- prattle likely grew from it with a playful diminutive ending.

Word Choice
